title: Compter, mesurer et indiquer un rang
summary: Build everyday and large numbers, read decimal commas, use prices per unit and distinguish cardinal labels from ordinal rank.
objectives: Build numbers from zero through hundreds and large units.
Apply `cent/vingt/mille` agreement and accepted hyphenation variants.
Read decimal notation and prices per unit.
Form ordinals and recognise contexts that use cardinal labels.

sections.title: Build a number from a small set of words
paragraphs: Learn 0–16: `zéro`, `un`, `deux`, `trois`, `quatre`, `cinq`, `six`, `sept`, `huit`, `neuf`, `dix`, `onze`, `douze`, `treize`, `quatorze`, `quinze`, `seize`. Then 17–19 are `dix-sept`, `dix-huit`, `dix-neuf`. Tens through 60 are `vingt`, `trente`, `quarante`, `cinquante`, `soixante`. Add a unit: `vingt-deux`, `trente-trois`. Use `et un` for 21, 31, 41, 51 and 61: `vingt et un`. `Un` changes to `une` when directly counting a feminine noun: `vingt et une personnes`.

Traditional spelling links many parts with hyphens but leaves spaces around `et` and between hundreds and following parts. The 1990 recommendations also allow hyphens throughout a compound numeral: `vingt-et-un`, `deux-cent-trente`. Both spelling systems are accepted in this course; exercises list legitimate variants rather than calling one wrong.
points: A number usually replaces an indefinite article before a noun: `deux livres`, not `des deux livres`.

examples.french: Il y a **vingt et une** places.

mistakes.why: `Un` becomes `une` when counting a feminine noun.

sections.title: In the common France/Canada system, 70 and 90 build on 60 and 80
paragraphs: 70 = `soixante-dix`; 71 = `soixante et onze`; 72 = `soixante-douze`. Continue the teens after `soixante` through 79 = `soixante-dix-neuf`. 80 = `quatre-vingts`; 81 = `quatre-vingt-un`, without `et`; 90 = `quatre-vingt-dix`; 91 = `quatre-vingt-onze`; 99 = `quatre-vingt-dix-neuf`. Belgium and Switzerland also use `septante` and `nonante`, and parts of Switzerland use `huitante`. These are legitimate regional forms; a task specifying France/Canada forms is testing that named system, not their validity.

100 = `cent`; 200 = `deux cents`; 201 = `deux cent un`; 999 = `neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-neuf`. `Cent` and `vingt` take `-s` when multiplied and final in a cardinal numeral: `deux cents`, `quatre-vingts`. They lose that `-s` before a further number: `deux cent trois`, `quatre-vingt-deux`. Do not add `s` to `cent` when it is not multiplied: `cent`, `cent un`.
points: No `et` in 81 or 91 in this system.
`Cent` and `vingt` have special number agreement; most number words do not vary.

examples.french: Le billet coûte **soixante et onze** euros.
Il reste **quatre-vingts** places, puis **quatre-vingt-une** après une annulation.
examples.english: There are eighty places left, then eighty-one after a cancellation.
examples.note: Final `vingt` takes `s` at 80; it loses `s` before `une`.

examples.french: La salle a **deux cents** sièges; le théâtre en a **deux cent dix**.
examples.english: The room has two hundred seats; the theatre has two hundred and ten.

mistakes.why: 81 has no `et` in the France/Canada counting system.

sections.title: `Mille` stays unchanged; `million` and `milliard` are nouns
paragraphs: 1 000 = `mille`, not `un mille` for ordinary counting; 2 000 = `deux mille`. `Mille` is invariable. 1 000 000 = `un million`; 1 000 000 000 = `un milliard`, English one billion. `Million` and `milliard` take plural `s` and `de` before a following counted noun when the amount ends there: `deux millions d'euros`. Contrast `deux mille euros`, without `de`. Before `mille`, `cent` and `vingt` lose their plural `s`; before `million`, a noun, they can keep it: `deux cent mille`, `deux cents millions`.

French uses a comma as the decimal separator and normally a space to group thousands: 1 250,5. Read a decimal with `virgule`, followed by the decimal digits or the decimal part as a number when clear: 3,25 can be `trois virgule vingt-cinq` or `trois virgule deux cinq`. A zero after the comma must be preserved in value: 3,05 = `trois virgule zéro cinq`. Prices commonly use `euros` and `centimes` rather than `virgule`.
points: English billion = French `milliard`, not `billion` in ordinary contemporary usage.
Do not use a period as the French decimal separator in the written-number exercises.

examples.english: The village has three thousand inhabitants.
The project costs two million euros.
examples.note: `Million` is a plural noun followed by `de/d'`.

examples.english: 1.05 is read as one point zero five.
examples.note: The zero is part of the decimal value.

mistakes.why: `Mille` is invariable and does not require `de` before `euros`.

sections.title: A rank uses an ordinal; a label or price unit may not
paragraphs: Cardinal numbers count or label: `trois livres`, `page trois`, `chambre douze`. Ordinals give rank: `premier/première` (first), `deuxième` (second), `troisième`, `quatrième`, `cinquième`, `sixième`, `septième`, `huitième`, `neuvième`, `dixième`. Normally add `-ième`, dropping a final `e`; `cinq` adds `u`, `neuf` changes `f` to `v`. `Vingt et unième` is twenty-first; only first itself uses `premier/première`. `Second/seconde` is another valid form for second; it is not a grammatical error merely because a series continues.

French commonly uses cardinal labels where English may use an ordinal: `page vingt`, `leçon quatre`, `Louis quatorze` (written Louis XIV). Dates normally use cardinals except `le premier`; the calendar lesson develops this. A count like `deux jours` is different from rank `le deuxième jour`.

For a price per unit, French uses the definite article: `trois euros le kilo`, `deux euros la pièce`, `cinq euros les cent grammes`. This is a rate, not ownership. `Le kilo` (m.) is a kilogram, `une pièce` (f.) here means one item, `un gramme` (m.) a gram.
points: The gendered first forms are `premier` and `première`; most `-ième` forms have one spelling for both genders.

examples.english: It is the first door, on the third floor.

examples.french: La réponse est à la page **vingt**.
examples.english: The answer is on page twenty.
examples.note: A page number is a label, not a `vingt-ième` construction.

examples.french: Les pommes coûtent deux euros **le kilo**.
examples.english: The apples cost two euros per kilogram.

examples.french: Le fromage coûte quatre euros **les cent grammes**.
examples.english: The cheese costs four euros per hundred grams.
examples.note: The rate applies to a specified plural quantity.

mistakes.why: For first on its own, use `première` with a feminine noun.

sections.title: Distinguish a numerical count, a quantity noun and a rank
paragraphs: `Un millier` (m.) is a group or quantity of a thousand, often an approximate count in ordinary use. Like `million`, it is a noun: it can take plural `-s` and needs `de/d'` before the things counted. `Mille` is instead an invariable number used directly before the counted noun. Do not insert `de` after every large number.

`Un tiers` (m.) means one third of a whole; `troisième` gives position in a sequence. For rulers' numerical names, the usual cardinal reading has one important boundary: `Ier` is `premier`, as in Henri Ier. A later numeral is cardinal. The fraction and the label are not ordinary adjective agreement problems.

examples.french: Le fichier contient **mille** noms. Le dossier contient **un millier de** noms.
examples.english: The file contains a thousand names. The folder contains about a thousand names.
examples.note: `Un millier de` commonly presents the number as an approximate quantity; `mille` gives the numerical count.

examples.french: **Des milliers de** visiteurs arrivent en été.
examples.english: Thousands of visitors arrive in summer.

examples.french: **Un tiers de** la salle est fermé; **la troisième** porte reste ouverte.
examples.english: One third of the room is closed; the third door remains open.
examples.note: A share of the space is not a position in a sequence.

examples.french: Dans le livre, **Henri Ier** se lit **Henri premier**, et **Henri IV** se lit **Henri quatre**.
examples.english: In the book, Henri I is read as Henri the First, and Henri IV as Henri the Fourth.
examples.note: The English ordinal translation does not dictate the French numerical reading.

sections.title: Read the currency and preserve the value of the cents
paragraphs: In a euro price written with a decimal comma, two digits after the comma give the centimes. The zero in 8,05 matters: five centimes are not fifty. A common spoken reading names `euros` between the whole amount and the cents; a fully explicit reading uses `euros et ... centimes`. `Un euro` is singular, while an amount of two euros or more normally takes plural `euros`.

For ordinary written prices, a useful format is the amount with a decimal comma followed by the currency symbol: 8,05 €. The English decimal point and leading currency sign need not be copied. `Un euro` (m.) is a euro; `un centime` (m.) is a cent.

examples.french: Ce carnet coûte **huit euros et cinq centimes** : **8,05 €**.
examples.english: This notebook costs eight euros and five cents: €8.05.
examples.note: The cents are five, not fifty, despite the two written decimal places.

examples.english: The stamp costs one euro fifty.
examples.note: The shorter spoken price is 1,50 €; the noun `euro` stays singular after `un`.

practice.prompt: Read the delivery charge 14,09 € using the explicit pattern '... euros et ... centimes'. Write only the amount in words.
practice.explanation: The amount after the decimal comma is nine cents, not ninety.

practice.prompt: Choose euro or euros in the spoken price for 1,80 €: 'un ___ quatre-vingts'.
practice.explanation: The currency noun is singular after un; the cents do not change that agreement.

practice.prompt: Write the English price €23.70 in French notation. Use a decimal comma and place the € sign after the amount.
practice.explanation: The comma separates euros and cents. The currency symbol follows the amount in the requested format.

practice.prompt: Supply de or no word (write 'rien'): 'Des milliers ___ cartes sont triées.'
practice.explanation: Milliers is a quantity noun and needs de before cartes.

practice.prompt: Keep the count of 1,000 but replace 'un millier de' with the ordinary number: 'Un millier de graines'. Write the resulting noun phrase.
practice.explanation: Mille is invariable and directly precedes graines, without de.

practice.prompt: Choose tiers or troisième: 'Un ___ du budget finance les livres.'
practice.explanation: A share of the budget is a fraction, not a third position.

practice.prompt: Choose tiers or troisième for rank: 'La ___ équipe présente son projet.'
practice.explanation: The team occupies third position; it is not one third of another team.

practice.prompt: Write only the word pronounced for Ier in the ruler's name 'Henri Ier'.
practice.explanation: The first ruler uses the ordinal premier; this is the exception to the usual cardinal reading.

practice.prompt: Write only the French word pronounced for IV in the ruler's name 'Henri IV'.
practice.explanation: The later ruler's numeral is cardinal in French even though English says the Fourth.

practice.prompt: Write 18 in French words.
practice.explanation: 18 combines dix and huit.

practice.prompt: Write 70 using the France/Canada counting system.
practice.explanation: 70 is sixty plus ten in this system.

practice.prompt: Write 2,000 as a French numeral in words, not digits.
practice.explanation: Mille is invariable; both hyphenation systems are accepted.

practice.prompt: Supply the ordinal for first: 'la ___ fois'.
practice.explanation: Fois is feminine.

practice.prompt: Write 81 in words, using the France/Canada system and masculine un.
practice.explanation: No et; vingt loses s before another number.

practice.prompt: Write the cardinal number 200 in words.
practice.explanation: Multiplied cent takes s when final.

practice.prompt: Write 999 in words, using the France/Canada system.
practice.explanation: Cent and vingt have no s before following number words.

practice.prompt: Write 1,000,000,000 in French words.
practice.explanation: An English billion is un milliard.

practice.prompt: Supply the required link: 'trois millions ___ personnes'.
practice.explanation: Million is a noun and takes de before the counted noun.

practice.prompt: Write the French digit notation for English 4.07. Use the decimal comma.
practice.explanation: French uses a comma; keep the zero.

practice.prompt: Write the ordinal meaning fifth.
practice.explanation: Cinq adds u before -ième.

practice.prompt: Write the ordinal meaning ninth.
practice.explanation: Neuf changes f to v.

practice.prompt: Use the normal cardinal page label, writing 14 in words: 'page ___'.
practice.explanation: A page label uses a cardinal, not quatorzième.

practice.prompt: Supply the article meaning per in this price: 'six euros ___ kilo'.
practice.explanation: The masculine singular unit takes le.

practice.prompt: Write the number 21 before feminine personnes, in words only.
practice.explanation: Un becomes une before a feminine counted noun.

practice.prompt: Are septante and nonante legitimate regional French number words?
practice.explanation: They are standard in several French-speaking regions.

practice.prompt: Write the cardinal number 80 in words using the France/Canada system.
practice.explanation: Final multiplied vingt takes s.

practice.prompt: Read 2,05 using virgule and individual decimal digits. Write the words.
practice.explanation: The zero after the comma cannot be dropped.

practice.prompt: Supply the article: 'trois euros ___ cent grammes'.
practice.explanation: A rate per one hundred grams uses plural les.

practice.prompt: Write the ordinal meaning twenty-first, masculine.
practice.explanation: Use unième inside a compound ordinal, not premier.

practice.prompt: Replace the numbered label 'porte 9' with a phrase expressing ninth in a sequence. Begin with la, keep porte and write the ordinal in words.
practice.explanation: A rank places the ordinal before the noun; neuf changes f to v in neuvième.

production_task.prompt: Write a short market note: a quantity, a price per kilogram and which stall you will visit first. Write at least one number in words.
production_task.model_answer: Je prends deux kilos de pommes à trois euros le kilo. Je vais au premier stand.
production_task.translation: I am taking two kilograms of apples at three euros per kilogram. I am going to the first stall.
rubric: Use the definite article for a price unit.
